sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Three pedestrian traverses and one stationary overnight run

**Instrumentation:** Independent quartz timebases, fluxgate magnetometer, VLF receiver, barometric recorder, and paired environmental loggers

**Study boundary:** A coded riparian reach and its ordinary vehicle-access corridor; property and geographic identifiers are retained separately.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Timing residual:** Two isolated timebases accumulated the same 42-to-96-millisecond offset while passing through a roughly 220-metre survey band. Both returned to their established drift rates after removal.

**Field correlation:** The interval coincided with a low-amplitude change in the local magnetic background. No matching change appeared on the stationary reference package.

**Repeatability:** Direction and walking speed changed the duration of the observation but not its mapped entry and exit points.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Receiver coupling, temperature compensation error, buried utility material, and an unrecorded ferrous source remain plausible.

**Unresolved point:** Bench testing reproduced neither the shared offset nor its recovery profile. The report does not claim a change to civil time or a biological effect.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Localized instrument-correlation variance; source unconfirmed

**Action:** Maintain the reach as a passive comparison site and require redundant clocks for any later survey.

**Personnel control:** No exposure limitation is indicated beyond ordinary remote-field procedures.

sections.title: COORDINATE & ACCESS SCHEDULE
sections.summary: Location references and land-access documentation remain with the controlling office.
